Hi — thanks for the clear asks. Short answer up front: for a production-oriented Dedicated pool with 32k context and 70B-class model, we recommend starting with 3 x H100-80GB (baseline steady-state) with autoscaling to 5–6 GPUs for bursty loads, unless you quantize to int4 in which case 6–8 A100-80GB or 12+ L4-class GPUs can be considered.

Key drivers: model weights (float16) ~60GB resident, KV cache for 32k peaks adds ~18–24GB depending on kv per-token footprint (see attached). Quantization (int8) typically cuts model memory by ~40–50% (down to ~30–36GB), int4 can get you to ~18–24GB but performance/latency tradeoffs vary.

I attached a quick spreadsheet (helix_sizing_v1.xlsx) with per-GPU memory tallies and a couple of throughput estimates for single-request and small-batch serving. I’ll loop in Laura with the procurement details and Monica for cluster/ops-level questions.

Next steps: if you can confirm 95th percentile request length and target RPS (or concurrency) we’ll finalize a Dedicated configuration and a mutual action plan for procurement.

--- Internal notes (engineer-facing) ---
Summary of numbers in sheet (rounded):
- Model baseline (float16, 70B-class): ~60GB weights.
- KV cache per token (internal layout used by runtime): ~0.0006 GB/token (~0.6 MB/token).
  - Avg 5k tokens -> ~3GB KV cache.
  - Spike 25k tokens -> ~15GB KV cache.
  - Peak 32k target -> ~19.2GB KV cache.
- Float16 resident total at 32k peak = ~60 + 19.2 = ~79.2GB (requires 80GB-class GPU without model sharding).
- Using int8 quantization: model -> ~33GB, total w/32k KV -> ~52GB (fits on 80GB A100/H100 easily, can pack 1 model + KV).
- Using int4 quantization: model -> ~20GB, total w/32k KV -> ~39GB (enables smaller GPUs like L4 48GB or multiple per-node placement).

Operational recommendation (POC):
- Option A (no quant): Reserved pool: 3x H100-80 (steady) with autoscale +2 (burst to 5). This keeps latency tight (no model sharding) and simplifies cold-starts.
- Option B (int8): 4x A100-80 or 6x L4 with model pinned; autoscale to 8 for headroom. Good cost/latency balance.
- Option C (int4 aggressive): 8+ L4s or mix with A100; requires careful eval for quality/regression.

Operational notes:
- KV caching: enable prefix caching for repeated sessions and LRU eviction for long-tails. For Helix, we should set KV cache budget per model instance ~20GB and enable cross-request prefix sharing for fine-tuned endpoints.
- Fallbacks: route to a quantized variant when capacity constrained (redwood routing policy), fall back to a smaller context-length variant (16k) when KV memory is saturated.

I added memory_profile_notes.pdf with the assumptions and formulae. Please review and comment.

Ben

Helix — thanks, Monica raised a good point about the KV footprint. Updated guidance below (finalized for procurement):

Concise recommendation for procurement (tickets / PO):
- Default POC config (recommended) — conservative but low-risk:
  - Reserved: 3 x H100-80GB (Dedicated pool), autoscale +2 for bursts -> burst to 5 GPUs.
  - Rationale: float16 model ~60GB + KV allowance 20GB (covers 32k peaks and per-layer metadata) -> ~80GB needed to keep single-model resident without sharding. Best latency profile and simplest rollouts.

- Cost-optimized POC (if Helix will run quantized):
  - Int8 option: 4 x A100-80GB reserved, autoscale to 6. Model mem ~33GB + KV ~18GB -> fits with headroom for batching.
  - Int4 option (quality must be validated): 6–8 x L4-48GB or 6+ A100-80; model mem ~20GB + KV ~18GB -> ~38GB total. Good for scale but requires eval checklist.

Operational guardrails we will implement for the POC:
- KV budget per instance: 20GB by default, configurable per-route.
- Fallback policy: when the KV budget is reached we redirect to a quantized variant or shortened-context variant (16k) depending on SLO vs. quality priority.
- Eviction/long-session handling: LRU + per-session soft throttling for >50k tokens; ops alerting on sustained long-session usage.

1) Helix to confirm 95th percentile request length and expected concurrency by Jan 19.
2) Redwood to deliver final quote for Option A and Option B by Jan 20 (I’ll include cost delta and SLA notes).
3) Joint runbook review (KV policies + fallback dance) week of Jan 22.
4) Procurement PO targeted Jan 26 to begin Reserved capacity provisioning.
